node_definition.done_when: Read section 7 of the-ledger-is-one-file-per-run first. record_hold_checks in reckon/ledger.py opens or closes a hold and then calls write() on the whole aggregate, leaving a tracked file dirty that nothing commits. After the change, a hold check either writes the hold to a file of its own that no run row shares, or commits what it rewrote with a message naming the hold, as the roster write already does. Reuse that roster commit (_commit_roster_write in reckon/ledger.py), or one shared generalisation of it, rather than a second commit mechanism. The commit stages only the path it wrote through a pathspec-limited commit, so it never carries anything another writer staged. While the repository has a merge in progress (.git/MERGE_HEAD exists), it makes no commit, leaves the write in place and says so on stderr. tests/test_hold_check_leaves_the_tree_clean.py works only in a temporary git repository, never the real state directory. It closes a hold and asserts that git status --porcelain is empty afterwards and that the committed diff changes no run row. A second case opens a hold and asserts the same. Both fail at your base. A third case has a merge in progress and asserts that no commit is made. Existing tests reaching record_hold_checks, holds() and the roster commit keep passing; grep tests/ for each to build the gate. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/the-ledger-is-one-file-per-run/hold-check-leaves-the-tree-clean.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line as revision= followed by the full sha, and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
